texts.li:
A petition, in charcoal, on the back of a feed sack:

"We ask for a snow day. No chores. No lessons. Everybody outside. Signed {A_nameDef}, and also two grown-ups who said not to put their names."

It's the good kind of snow, too, the kind that packs.

{A_nameDef} woke the whole colony at dawn shouting that it had snowed. Now {A_nameDef} is standing in front of the council in three coats, asking for the day off for everyone, to build the biggest snowman the colony has ever seen.

[lowtech] First deep snow of the year. Where {A_nameDef}'s parents came from, that meant a holiday, with everyone out sliding on the hill and a hot drink after, and {A_nameDef} has already found a board to slide on.

li.label: A snow day for everyone
li.outcome: Out in the snow, all of them, for the middle of the day: {A_nameDef} built a snowman out in the open, and the rest stood round in the cold, stamping their feet. The work waited.

outcomes.li: [quirk:WrongLaugh] {A_nameDef} gave the snowman a crooked grin and couldn't stop laughing at it, and before long the whole colony was laughing too. The work waited.
[lowtech] They stood out in the snow round {A_nameDef}'s snowman until the cold drove them in, and called it the snow day, and decided it should happen every year.

li.label: The children can play; the rest of us work
li.outcome: The children had their snow day, and the grown-ups watched from the windows, working. Several grown-ups found reasons to go outside more often than usual.

li.label: Snow means more work, not less
li.outcome: Snow means paths to clear and roofs to sweep, so {A_nameDef} was handed a shovel. {A_nameDef} built a very small snowman by the path, on {A_possessive} own, out of spite.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has marked out a race course round the fields with sticks and string, and wants the whole colony to come and watch the children run it one evening. There will be a prize. The prize is to be decided.

{A_nameDef} says {A_pronoun} is the fastest runner in the colony and wants it settled properly: a race, all the children, everyone watching, at midsummer. The other children have agreed, with conditions.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} wants to run the bounds of the fields, the whole way round, the way the children of {A_possessive} family did every summer so they'd know their land. With the grown-ups cheering, if the council allows.

li.label: Everyone comes out to cheer
li.outcome: The whole colony lined the course one long summer evening and cheered the children round it. {A_nameDef} came second, and argued about it until the stars were out. The prize was a honey cake, shared.

outcomes.li: [quirk:Volunteers] {A_nameDef} volunteered to run, to keep the course, to hand out the prize and to tidy up afterward. {A_nameDef} came third, and was the happiest of anyone.

li.label: The children can race on their own
li.outcome: The children ran their race with only each other to cheer. {A_nameDef} won, according to {A_nameDef}.

li.label: No time for races this summer
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took the string down from the course and coiled it very slowly, where the council could see.

texts.li: The harvest is in, and {A_nameDef} has noticed how much is left lying in the stubble. {A_nameDef} asks if the children could glean the fields after the harvesters, and have what they find counted as their own.
{A_nameDef} has a basket and a plan: every child in the colony walks the harvested fields and picks up what was missed, and whatever they find is the children's own.
[lowtech] In the old days, {A_nameDef} has been told, the gleanings belonged to the children and the poor, by right. {A_nameDef} would like that to be true here too.

li.label: The gleanings are the children's
li.outcome: The children combed the stubble with baskets and came back with more than anyone expected. The grown-ups met them at the field's edge to look, and were told, very seriously and at length, who had found what.

li.label: Glean, but it goes to the stores
li.outcome: The children gleaned the fields and everything went into the storeroom. {A_nameDef} carried in the last basket and put it down with a sigh that could be heard across the colony.

li.label: The animals can have the stubble
li.outcome: The stubble went to the animals. {A_nameDef} picked one perfect ear of grain on the way back and kept it on {A_possessive} windowsill.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} wants to plant a tree. Not just any tree: {A_possessive} tree, at the edge of the fields, with {A_possessive} name on a stone beside it. And then every child gets one. {A_nameDef} has thought this through.

{A_nameDef} found a sapling growing in a crack by the wall and wants to give it a proper home. The idea grew in the telling: every spring, every child plants a tree, and the colony grows a grove of them.
[lowtech] You could tell anyone's age by their tree, where {A_nameDef}'s mother grew up: every child planted one the first spring they could walk. {A_nameDef} would like to start that here.

li.label: Every child plants a tree
li.outcome: The colony walked out to the edge of the fields one spring morning, and every child planted a sapling and put a stone beside it. {A_nameDef} watered {A_possessive} twice before breakfast and once after.

outcomes.li: [quirk:SoftSpot] {A_nameDef} planted {A_possessive} tree and then spent the rest of the morning building a little fence round it to keep the animals off, then left a pile of scraps outside the fence for them, as an apology.

li.label: the planting of the children's trees
Just {A_nameDef}'s tree, this year
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} planted {A_possessive} tree by the wall, alone, with a stone beside it. It's very small. {A_nameDef} says it'll be the tallest in the colony one day.

li.label: Trees take room from the crops
li.outcome: The land is for crops, the council said. {A_nameDef} planted the sapling in a pot by {A_possessive} bed instead, and talks to it.
